title: Cross-Team Signalboard — Staff Notes 2027-11-17
content:
Purpose:
Quick cross-team sync to capture operational signals, triangular issues that need multi-team follow-up, and key decisions for the week. Treat this as the source-of-truth for action items from 2027-11-17 staff meeting.

Attendees (approx):
- Aisha Patel (serving runtime lead)
- Liam Chen (platform eng)
- Marisol Rivera (SRE)
- Omar Haddad (private deployments)
- Priya Kapoor (product: hosted API)
- Ben Carter (solutions eng)
- Eva Liu (observability, joined for metrics)

Agenda Quick Notes:
1) Operational signals & incidents (last 7d)
2) Dedicated capacity anomaly follow-up
3) KV-cache regression observation and rollback plan
4) Private deployment onboarding cadence + checklist gaps
5) Rollouts: quantization profile canary next steps
6) Action items and owners

1) Operational signals & incidents
- Incident summary: On 11/14 early morning, a Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 showed sustained P95 token latency increases (~2.2x baseline) for ~45 minutes. Root cause preliminary: inter-node networking flaps coincident with a kernel update on a subset of nodes in the pool. Impact: 3 enterprise customers saw degraded tail latency and several active streams timed out and retried.
- Current status: kernel hotfix rolled to affected nodes, auto-healing triggered; full mitigation confirmed 11/15 03:20 UTC. Ongoing: SRE has a post-mortem in draft (JIRA-SERV-4821).
- Notes: customers affected have been contacted by CS; product offered temporary credits. PR to add additional healthcheck gating for kernel updates is in review (PR 1782).

2) Dedicated capacity anomaly follow-up
- Action from last week: create capacity heatmap and alert threshold for cross-node latency skew. Heatmap (weekly) shows occasional skew tied to kernel/firmware patch windows.
- Platform engineering will: a) add node-level patch gating (prevent patching during sustained high-util windows), b) attach a pre-patch smoke test that exercises inter-node RPC paths.
- Timeline: initial gating implemented by 11/23 (Liam), smoke-test infra by 11/30 (platform-eng + infra).

3) KV-cache regression observation and rollback plan
- Observation: After last runtime release (v1.48.0) we saw increased CPU pressure for certain long-prefix workloads—signal points to a change in the KV-cache eviction heuristic.
- Immediate mitigation: revert heuristic change on a canary ring for low-risk models to validate. Marisol to coordinate canary with SRE.
- Risk: rollback may increase memory footprint; need to confirm Dedicated pool memory headroom before wide rollback. Omar to provide Dedicated pool headroom snapshot by 11/19.

4) Private deployment onboarding cadence + checklist gaps
- Customer feedback: onboarding checklist missing explicit KMS/HSM test step and VPC egress rule validation. Also docs ambiguous around local metrics retention config.
- Decision: temporarily add a "security & networking" gate to the onboarding template. Priya to update onboarding doc and surface to sales/solutions eng.
- Deliverables: updated checklist (docs PR) by 11/24; a short runbook for KMS validation by 11/29. Owner: Priya + Ben.

5) Rollouts: quantization profile canary next steps
- Background: Optimize recommended a new INT8-compatible quantization profile that promises 20% cost reduction for NLU-heavy customers but showed small BLEU/regression on a small eval set.
- Plan: proceed with staged canary — 1) offline eval re-run on expanded evalsets (today), 2) controlled canary on non-production traffic (11/19), 3) limited customer opt-in canary (11/26).
- Quality guardrails: automated eval threshold must pass with no more than 0.8% delta on key metrics; any customer-reported quality regression to trigger immediate fallback.

6) Observability and Metrics
- Eva highlighted gaps: tracer sampling inconsistent for streaming sessions; cost attribution for streaming tokens not accurately mapped to model variant when fallbacks occur.
- Quick wins: normalize trace tags for model_variant and fallback_reason by 11/22 (observability). Longer work: refactor billing attribution pipeline (Q1).

Decisions taken
- Add node-level patch gating for Dedicated clusters (see above).
- Insert "security & networking" gate into private onboarding checklist.
- Proceed with quantization canary under tightened guardrails.

Action items (owner — due date — status notes)
- Liam Chen — implement node-level patch gating (11/23) — in_progress.
- Marisol Rivera — schedule KV-cache canary and coordinate with SRE (11/19) — pending headroom report.
- Omar Haddad — Dedicated pool headroom snapshot + mem headroom flag (11/19) — pending.
- Priya Kapoor & Ben Carter — update onboarding checklist and produce KMS runbook (11/24, 11/29) — drafting.
- Eva Liu — normalize trace tags for model_variant & fallback_reason (11/22) — TODO.
- Aisha Patel — consolidate post-mortem draft and finalize communications to affected customers (11/18) — in_review.

Parking lot / lower priority items
- Investigate automated fallback selection to prefer model variants with larger KV caches for long-prefix workloads.
- Explore bandwidth-aware routing for private deployments crossing region boundaries.

Questions / open concerns
- Q: Can we provide a short-term memory safety toggle for customers wanting the older KV heuristic? (Benefit: quick customer-level rollback) — Needs engineering estimate.
- Q: Is there appetite to freeze kernel patches in Dedicated pools during peak hours (customer-facing windows)? Platform asks for a narrow definition of "peak" — propose 08:00-18:00 PST M-F for now; Liam to propose final policy by 11/23.

Notes to self / roughs
- Reminder: follow up with CS on messaging template for regressions (short + technical + compensation options).
- Put a small slot in next week's agenda for "rollouts post-mortem" (quantization learnings).

Next meeting focus (2027-11-24)
- Post-mortem review for us-west-2 Dedicated incident
- KV-cache canary results and decision
- Canary results for quantization profile, and next steps

Appendix / quick refs (tickets mentioned)
- JIRA-SERV-4821 (Dedicated cluster latency incident)
- JIRA-OPS-5109 (Patch gating infra epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1782 (pre-patch healthcheck)

End of notes.

Scratch / informal snippets: 
- "we really need better pre-patch smoke tests — rolling kernel is basically a blunderbuss"
- "customer ops appreciated the proactive credits, but CS asks for runbook text for next time"
- TODO: ask product to prioritize billing-attribution fix for streaming tokens in Q1 roadmap planning meeting
